name: adapters
description: The adapter contract, plus a reference adapter. The receipts wire-format constants live in a Go package compiled into spex; the adapters themselves are scripts outside the binary. Each adapter consumes changeset.json, executes the tool-specific subcommands against a bead tracker, and writes receipts.json. The current reference adapter targets br (beads_rust); authors of adapters for other trackers (bd, GitHub Issues, Jira) consult the same changeset/receipts contracts without changes to spex. Requirements in this module double as the contract any adapter must satisfy.

requirements.title: Read changeset v1
requirements.description: The adapter parses changeset.json v1 and refuses earlier or later versions with a clear error. It reads ops in the order given and processes them sequentially — order matters because later ops may forward-reference earlier op results.

requirements.title: Op ID substitution table
requirements.description: As the adapter processes create ops, it maintains an op_id → bead_id substitution table. When a later op's deps or parent contains {"ref":"op","op_id":"<id>"}, the adapter resolves the ref from this table. Missing table entries (e.g., the referenced op was skipped or errored) cause the dependent op to be downgraded to error with a clear reason.

requirements.title: Resolve three ref shapes
requirements.description: For each ref field in parent and deps: {"ref":"bead","bead_id":"<id>"} resolves as-is; {"ref":"op","op_id":"<id>"} resolves via the substitution table; {"ref":"spec_node","spec_node_id":"<id>"} resolves via a live lookup to the spex mapping store (.bead-map.json) for the most recent bead_id associated with that spec_node_id.

requirements.title: Idempotent create via label
requirements.description: Before creating a bead for a create op, the adapter queries the tracker for an existing open bead carrying the op's idempotency.label (spex:<record-id> on ordinary creates, spex:cleanup-<spec_node_id> on cleanup creates); the adapter treats the label as opaque and does not parse it. On match: skip the create, record was_existing=true with the existing bead_id in the receipt. On no match: create the bead, record was_existing=false with the new bead_id. Re-runs of a partial changeset are safe: already-created beads are not duplicated.

requirements.title: Idempotent close via label
requirements.description: Before closing a bead for a close op, the adapter checks whether the target bead already carries the spex:obsolete label. If yes: skip the close, record status=skipped with reason="already obsoleted". If no: close the bead with the spex:obsolete and commit:<HEAD> labels. This guards against the crash-between-close-and-receipt scenario — a second run sees the bead is already labeled and records the skip correctly.

requirements.title: Write receipts v1
requirements.description: For each op processed (or failed), the adapter records a per-op entry with op_id, status (ok|skipped|error), bead_id (if applicable), was_existing (for create ops), and an optional error or reason string. The entries are accumulated and receipts.json is written once, after the last op. The top-level status field is complete if every op produced ok or intentional-skipped, partial if any op resulted in error. An adapter that exits before the last op writes no receipts file at all; spex ingest then fails with ingest: read receipts: ... no such file or directory and exit 1, so an aborted adapter run must be re-run, not ingested.

requirements.title: Integration test against real br
requirements.description: A shell-based integration test (scripts/apply-br_test.sh) exercises the full adapter against a real br sandbox. It validates: changeset parsing, all three ref shapes resolving correctly, idempotency on re-run, receipt output matches the v1 schema, and partial-receipt handling when a synthetic failure is injected mid-run. The test is gated on br being present on PATH and is excluded from the Go test suite.

requirements.title: Reference implementation scope
requirements.description: scripts/apply-br.sh is explicitly marked as a reference implementation — vet before production use. It demonstrates the required adapter contract but does not aspire to handle every tracker misconfiguration. Users wanting production-grade adapters for their environment should fork and adapt. The contract (this module's functional requirements) is the authoritative specification that any adapter must meet.

components.name: BrReferenceAdapter
components.description: Bash + jq implementation of the adapter contract targeting br (beads_rust). Ships at scripts/apply-br.sh. Reads changeset.json, resolves refs via the substitution table, runs br create/list/show/update/close for each op, and writes receipts.json. Integration-tested against a real br sandbox via scripts/apply-br_test.sh.

data_flows.name: Adapter flow
data_flows.description: changeset.json → parse → iterate ops in order → for each op: resolve refs, query tracker for idempotency, run subcommand, record receipt → receipts.json assembled in memory and written atomically once, after the last op, so a reader sees either the whole document or the path's previous contents; a run that dies mid-loop writes nothing, and spex ingest then fails with ingest: read receipts: ... no such file or directory and exit 1, so an aborted run must be re-run rather than ingested.
